### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**11** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them. ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/translation.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/automation.json`, `packages/spec/export-origins/automation.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/translation.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **68** of **251** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **183** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **183**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **124** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **175** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json abe95a950dc2fa93c49120b624129783ef818373` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c37dddbba9f4615650252f7daa86de2f835e0fba` — the merge of head `6f3b8c88b32cf4f61ef3913007f46c4fe4ac4f04` into base `abe95a950dc2fa93c49120b624129783ef818373`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c37dddbba9f4615650252f7daa86de2f835e0fba && git checkout c37dddbba9f4615650252f7daa86de2f835e0fba
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin abe95a950dc2fa93c49120b624129783ef818373 6f3b8c88b32cf4f61ef3913007f46c4fe4ac4f04 && git checkout -B drift-repro abe95a950dc2fa93c49120b624129783ef818373 && git merge --no-ff 6f3b8c88b32cf4f61ef3913007f46c4fe4ac4f04

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json abe95a950dc2fa93c49120b624129783ef818373
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `6f3b8c88b32cf4f61ef3913007f46c4fe4ac4f04`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/flow-altitude.ts, packages/spec/src/automation/index.ts, packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts + packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts, packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/basic/flow-branches.ts, ui/packages/components/src/renderers/basic/metadata-viewer.tsx, ui/packages/i18n/src/flowLabels.ts

Inputs read: card #36530 (body and its 4 comments), PR #36576 (body, 17-file list, net diff against merge-base `87c7bbaf`), and the 75 check-runs on this head: all completed, none failed, none pending (success or expected skip; Check Changeset, Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Spec property liveness, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Test Core, Test UI all `success`). Tests, the generated files (api-surface, export-origins, liveness, translation.mdx) and the rest are the lane seat's ACCEPT; the changeset is read under ② only.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Accept-set, `objectstack validate` (widening) — right.** `flows.FLOW.nodes.NODE_ID.label` is now accepted over a screen whose `config.title` is a non-empty string (`ScreenFacts.titled`: a string of non-zero length). The fact is collected in `collectFlowRecord` through `walkFlowNodes`, so it holds at any depth (ADR-0031 regions included), the same universe the `nodes` loop judges against. An untitled screen is still refused with `translation-target-unknown` and pointed at `screens.NODE_ID.title`; an approval is still pointed at `approvals.NODE_ID.label`; an unknown id is still refused and its did-you-mean list now offers titled screens. Nothing that was accepted on main is refused at this head.
- **"Titled" predicate across the four readers — right on every schema-valid config.** `ScreenConfigSchema.title` is `z.string().optional()`, so the value is a string or absent. Validator: non-empty string. `flowStepName`: `typeof title === 'string' && title`. `stepLabel`: not `undefined` / `null` / `''`. Walk: a string holding `{{` (a subset, by design). A whitespace-only title is "titled" in all four. See N3 for the one spelling difference, unreachable through the schema.
- **Translation schema face — right.** `translation.zod.ts` changes prose and two `.describe` strings only; the `nodes` group is still `z.record(string, strictObject({ label }))`. No parse verdict moves. The new prose (an untitled screen and an approval excluded, a titled screen keyed here, heading stays `screens.NODE_ID.title`) matches the validator and both readers sentence by sentence.
- **Public surface, `@objectstack/spec/automation` (additive) — right.** `flowDecisionEdgeBranch`, `FlowDecisionEdgeBranch`, `FLOW_DECISION_DEFAULT_BRANCH_LABEL` exported by name from `flow-altitude.ts`; the api-surface and export-origins rows name the same three with the same origins. Nothing removed or renamed.
- **Public surface, `@object-ui/i18n` `stepLabel` (behaviour) — right.** A titled screen moves from `undefined` to its `nodes` value; an untitled screen whose translated title holds `{{` moves from the raw template to `undefined`. All three consumers at this head draw `stepLabel(node) ?? authored` (`FlowCanvas.tsx:1300`, `flow-region-view.tsx:102`, and the inspector heading in `FlowPreview.tsx:175`, which the PR body does not name but which behaves the same way), so none can draw `undefined`.
- **Coverage demand (`collectExpectedEntries`) — right, with one stated limit.** The walk newly asks for the `nodes` key on a top-level screen whose authored `config.title` holds `{{`. This is the walk's own documented rule for the `nodes` family (the label of every step the docs embed draws at `detail: business`); the Studio canvas reading a wider set does not widen it, exactly as for technical steps and region-nested nodes, which the canvas also draws and the walk has never asked for. The walk is locale-independent, so it tests the authored heading while the embed tests the heading in the reader's language; a translation that removes or adds a hole moves what the embed draws in that one locale without moving the demand. That is inherent in a static walk and is not a finding.
- **Branch rule — a faithful extraction; no edge's verdict moves in either reader.** Checked case by case against main: non-record edge (skipped before, `undefined` now); `isDefault === true` (default in both); no declared conditions (every out-edge, including one labelled `default`, listed in both; the viewer's guard is still `guardOf(edge.condition)`); declared conditions with the `default` label (default); a string label a condition claims (condition, same `find`); anything else left out. The conditions filter (`Array.isArray` then plain records) is the same expression both readers carried. Against the engine (`logic-nodes.ts` decision executor, `dag-traversal.ts` `traverseNext`): the declared-conditions route (first matching condition's label, else `default`, also claimed by an `isDefault` edge) and the gateway route (edge conditions, `isDefault` as fall-through) are what the three kinds describe. The divergences that exist are pre-existing and carried over verbatim; see N1.
- **Runtime — nothing reads the key for a screen, and nothing needs to.** `translateFlow` overlays the flow label, terminal messages and screen nodes only, and is deliberately not registered in `translateMetadataDocument`, so no served read translates a node label; `protocol-translated-echo.ts` has no flow slot and needs none. The engine's screen executor reads `screens.NODE_ID.title` / `.description` only. The key is display-only, as the zod prose and the liveness note say.

### ② Semver level

Clause-②: yes (widening) — agrees with the diff: the only accept-set movement is the validator accepting a key it refused, plus additive exports. No narrowing arm is owed.

`Metadata-protocol: added` is the right kind: a translation-bundle key an author can now write over a titled screen where `objectstack validate` refused it. The kind sets the level at `minor` on each package the diff moves, and the changeset carries `minor` on `@objectstack/spec` (new exports, schema prose), `@objectstack/lint` (validator, walk), `@object-ui/i18n` (`stepLabel`) and `@object-ui/components` (`flowStepName`, `decisionBranches`). `@objectstack/cli` and `@object-ui/app-shell` move by test files only and publish nothing. The changeset and PR body both carry the two declaration lines; `Check Changeset` is `success` on this head. The changeset body matches the tree bullet by bullet, including the honest statement that coverage asks only on a top-level screen with a holed heading.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions`: empty in the dev report; nothing to answer.
- Dev deviations (push 2 before its overlap-check; `origin/main` not merged before opening; report posted after the PR): process only, no contract effect; `mergeable_state` is `clean`.
- Out-of-scope note, engine keeps its own `DEFAULT_BRANCH_LABEL`: answered under N2.
- Key name (`nodes.NODE_ID.label` rather than a `screens.NODE_ID.label` member): the seat's call in claim 7086969804, and it holds. `screens` aliases `label` onto `title`, so that spelling already means the heading; the `nodes` group's own rule ("every node whose label has no key of its own") covers a titled screen's label without a new member. One string keeps one key: heading under `screens`, label under `nodes`.
- ADR sentences ride #36086 and skill text rides #36401 (`Skills-docs: follow-up #36401`); no `docs/adr/**` or `skills/**` path is in the diff, so neither is judged here.
- SQL push-down: none. The diff touches no query, no id materialisation and no in-app join.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/automation/flow-altitude.ts`** — holds. Against its first consumers: both `decisionBranches` and `decisionBranchTechnicalTargets` now call it and both private `'default'` constants are gone, which is what comment 7084469163 asked for. It is a pure function over `unknown`, so no UI guard type entered the spec. The three kinds map one-to-one onto the viewer's guards (`otherwise` / the edge's own condition / the claimed condition's expression) and the walk needs only truthiness. Tried to break it: a `default`-labelled edge on a gateway is an ordinary edge (correct: the engine reports no branch label there); `conditions` holding only non-records degrades to a gateway in both readers as before; an array passed as `edge` is refused by `isPlainRecord`.

**`packages/spec/src/automation/index.ts`** — holds. Named exports beside `FLOW_TECHNICAL_NODE_TYPES`, `type` modifier on the type; api-surface and export-origins agree; Type Check gates green.

**`packages/spec/src/system/translation.zod.ts`** — holds against ruling 7076440876 ("every drawn step can carry a label per language") and its first consumers. Each sentence checked in the tree: "at any depth" (validator universe is `walkFlowNodes`); "the Studio canvas draws it" (`FlowCanvas`, `RegionNode` via `stepLabel`); "the docs embed draws it where the heading holds a hole, elsewhere names the screen by its heading" (`flowStepName` at this head); "`objectstack validate` points a `nodes` key over either at its own key" (untitled screen and approval branches of the `nodes` block).

**`packages/lint/src/validate-translation-references.ts`** — agrees. The `titled` skip runs before the type test, so a titled screen is accepted and an untitled one still reaches the redirect; the new message says why ("no `config.title` of its own, so its label is its heading").

**`packages/lint/src/i18n-walk.ts`** — agrees. The screen arm demands the key exactly where `flowStepName` falls to the label for the authored heading; the nested case is not demanded, consistent with the comment and the validator's wider accept. The branch-target loop is the old loop with the predicate swapped.

**`ui/packages/components/src/renderers/basic/metadata-viewer.tsx`** — agrees. Heading test first: a plain (translated or authored) heading names a titled screen even when a `nodes` key exists; a holed heading falls to `stepLabel` (the `nodes` key), then the authored label, then the id. An untitled screen takes the `stepLabel` path unchanged. With no bundle, `translated` is undefined and the authored values are drawn.

**`ui/packages/i18n/src/flowLabels.ts`** — agrees. The untitled arm returns inside its block (a missing or holed translated title answers `undefined` and never falls through to the `nodes` key, which validate refuses there); a titled screen falls out to the `nodes` read. Item (e): an untitled screen whose translated title holds a hole draws the authored label in the canvas (`?? node.label`), the inspector and the embed alike.

**`ui/packages/components/src/renderers/basic/flow-branches.ts`** — agrees; see ① for the case table.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 (nit) — `flowDecisionEdgeBranch`'s jsdoc says `undefined` is "an edge no branch can ever take". In the engine that holds only while every computed label is claimed: when a decision's branch label has no claiming out-edge, `traverseNext` logs a warning and evaluates every out-edge, the unlisted ones included; the engine also drops `type: 'fault'` out-edges, which neither drawing filters; and on a conditions decision an `isDefault` edge loses to a `default`-labelled sibling. All three are pre-existing in `decisionBranches` on main and moved verbatim, so no verdict changes here. Now that the rule is a published spec export, soften the sentence ("an edge the decision's own branch labels never select") or carry the engine parity on a follow-up card.

N2 (nit) — `FLOW_DECISION_DEFAULT_BRANCH_LABEL` and the engine's `DEFAULT_BRANCH_LABEL` are two copies of one word, joined only by a jsdoc sentence. That is the same shape comment 7084469163 removed between lint and UI. `service-automation` already imports `@objectstack/spec`, so the engine can read the spec constant; out of this card's file surface, so a follow-up card (the dev noted it with `carrier: none`).

N3 (nit) — "titled" is spelled two ways: a non-empty string in the validator and `flowStepName`, "not undefined / null / empty string" in `stepLabel`. They differ only for a non-string `config.title`, which `ScreenConfigSchema` refuses, so no served or validated flow can show the difference. One shared predicate would close it; accepted deviation or follow-up.
